summary: Duncan Ryūken Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. His career includes posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Boston University by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Trashichöling, Sera, and Gyuto Monasteries under teachers including Ngawang Yönten. He held professorships and leadership posts at Minzu University of China, Tibet University, TASS, and CTRC.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College (~1934–1952), Sanskrit College and University (1952), and the University of Calcutta.

Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Lucknow, studying under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri as well as R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

Dwarikadas Shastri was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Bauddhadarśanācārya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He founded Bauddha Bharati and served as a joint editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha was a historian and Indologist who studied at Patna University, Presidency University (~1956–1960), and the University of Calcutta (~1961–1964).
Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD in 2018 at KU Leuven, where he also served as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and served as a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He directed Nitartha Institute (~1996) and served as director at Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

Dániel Balogh works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He has been affiliated with the British Museum (attested 2021) and served as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, with Helmut Tauscher supervising her MA.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry is an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer. He served as a lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Kerala (attested 1973).

E. F. Schumacher was a philosopher who studied at New College, London School of Economics, University of Bonn, and Columbia University under Edward Conze. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1933–1934) and the University of Oxford.

E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist who studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, University of Utah, and University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He worked at the Library of Congress and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~1999–2010).

E. Michael Mendelson was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He was educated at the University of Cambridge (King's College) (~1948–1952), the University of Paris (~1952–1956), and the University of Chicago (~1956–1963).
E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1951–1954) and held a post at Sri Venkateswara University (~1964–1982).

E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he served as principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who completed his PhD at the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and president of Rietberg-Gesellschaft (~2001).
